name: TEER robot
full_name: Boston Children's robotic drive for transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral repair (MitraClip cartridges on a universal catheter drive)
group: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (P. E. Dupont; L. Pistorius, N. U. Nayar, P. Tran) with UCSF (S. Elmariah)
versions: 2025 arXiv; 2026 RAL; the universal drive itself is announced for a separate letter
devices_driven: Abbott MitraClip NTR through an Edwards PASCAL Precision transseptal sheath; manual handles replaced by transmission cartridges (Sec. II)
n_dof_detail: 8 used (transseptal sheath 3, intermediate sheath 3, device sheath 2); drive supports up to four telescoping sheaths with up to four motorised inputs each
rotation_detail: motor-driven worm gears for bending and rotation; clamp on the handle for device-sheath roll
haptics_leader: game controller (haptic device input supported by the ROS 2 software)
validation_detail: silicone mitral model (United Biologics); one operator; 5 manual and 5 robotic trials per step test; 30 manual and 30 robotic clip deliveries, 10 per segment A1P1, A2P2, A3P3 (Sec. IV)
key_numbers: segment 2 robotic time 52% of manual; mean clip placement error from 3 mm to below 1 mm for segments 2 and 3; inadvertent clip rotation 28 +- 4 deg manual vs 6 +- 7 deg robotic; speed limits 5.46 deg/s flexure, 14.56 deg/s roll, 6 mm/s translation
